amendments.rule: The conjunction `וְ` is normally English *and*, including the waw of a consecutive verb form: the conjunction takes *And* and the verb takes the verb. Where the ASV renders it by some other connective, align it to that word instead. **The list is open and is read off the ASV rather than checked against a set**: the corpus already aligns a waw to *but*, *then*, *so*, *or*, *now*, *also*, *for*, *therefore*, *neither*, *nor*, *yea*, *yet*, *even*, *with*, *moreover* and *howbeit*, among others. A connective the ASV has written for a waw is never `added`, and it is never folded into a neighbouring word to avoid one: a town list writes *with* for the waw of `וְחַצְרֵיהֶן` → *with their villages* and *even* for the waw of `וָיָמָּה` → *even unto the sea*, and each waw takes the word written for it. **Where the ASV renders one waw by a correlative pair such as *both … and* or *either … or*, both English words belong to the waw's one discontinuous unit, headed on the closing connective (*and* or *or*); the opening correlative is not `added`.** **But that governs only a pair no other morpheme has a claim on.** Where another morpheme standing in the clause is itself what the opening correlative says — a present negative for the *neither* of *neither … nor*, the `מִן` of a `מִן … עַד` range for the *both* of *both … and* — that morpheme takes the opening word and the waw takes only the closing connective, exactly as rule 47 gives a written *the* to a present article before a supplied one and rule 46 gives a *that* to a present relative before a bare participle. `אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יָדְעוּ הֵמָּה וַאֲבוֹתָם` → *whom* ***neither*** *they* ***nor*** *their fathers have known* gives *neither* to `לֹא` and *nor* to the waw, and `מֵעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָה` → ***both*** *the birds of the heavens* ***and*** *the beasts* gives *both* to `מִן` and *and* to the waw, leaving the `עַד` `unrepresented` under rule 40. Count the correlative's members against the morphemes that could carry them, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s. This does not touch rule 35's fusion, which is a single English word carrying every morpheme's sense: a lone *Nor* or *neither* with no answering *nor* written is that rule's, and only a written pair is this one's. Read what stands in the clause for that waw in particular, as rule 51 requires for *also*, and where the ASV leaves it unrendered, mark it `unrepresented`. **But read whether a waw is present at all before placing the connective.** Where the ASV writes a coordinating *and*, *or* or *but* for a clause or phrase in which no conjunction morpheme stands, no morpheme licenses that word and it is its own `added` unit under rule 30. Hebrew juxtaposes where English coordinates, and the ASV supplies the connective freely: `עַל־כָּתֵף תִּשָּׂא בָּעֲלָטָה תוֹצִיא` → *shalt thou bear it upon thy shoulder,* ***and*** *carry it forth in the dark* writes one for a clause the Hebrew leaves asyndetic, and `לְיוֹשְׁבֵי יְרוּשָׁלִַם אֶל־אַדְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל` → *concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem* ***and*** *the land of Israel* writes one for a second prepositional phrase the Hebrew merely sets beside the first. Do not fold such a word into the preposition, the verb or the noun standing next to it to avoid the `added`, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and* and rule 51 about a supplied *also*: the word is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them, and a preposition whose own relation the ASV has left unstated is `unrepresented` under rule 40 rather than a home for a coordinator. Count the clause's conjunctions against the ASV's connectives, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s, and mark whichever side is in surplus. Read the clause before counting, since a morpheme that has an English word of its own is not made a surplus by this sentence: a present negative carries a *nor* or a *neither* under rule 35, a `כִּי` or an `אִם` carries a *but* or an *or* the ASV has written for it, and only a connective no morpheme answers to is `added`.
amendments.why: This chapter met the case three times — EZK.12.6 t011, 12.7 t039 and 12.19 t019 — and the contract as written did not prevent the error: the verse pass on 12.19 folded the supplied *and* into the אֶל beside it, and only reconciliation caught it. Rule 51 already forbids that fold for a supplied *also* and rule 42 for a surplus *and* between numerals, but rule 42's whole frame is the numeral phrase, so a coordinating *and* written where Hebrew juxtaposes had no address. Rule 14 is where it belongs, because it is the rule that decides what a waw's connective is and it already closes by telling the reader to look at what stands in the clause for that waw in particular. The addition is scoped to mirror rule 51's structure exactly — it applies only where no waw is present — and its closing sentence protects rule 35's *Nor* and the כִּי/אִם connectives from being read as surpluses. Nothing in the corpus contradicts it; the corpus tables are keyed by source lemma and so contain no `added` units to weigh either way, which is why the evidence carrying this is the three units here and the reasoning rules 42 and 51 already state for their own connectives.

conventions: אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה is split three ways wherever it stands (12.10, 12.19, 12.23, 12.25, 12.28): אֲדֹנָי takes *the Lord* with the supplied *the* under rule 15, its 1cs suffix is `unrepresented` because the ASV writes no pronoun for it, and יְהוִה takes *Jehovah*. In נְאֻם אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה the ASV recasts נְאֻם as the finite *saith*, so no *of* is written for the construct relation and none is placed. BSB represents that suffix and this is the documented difference, not an error.

לְעֵינֵיהֶם, seven times across 12.3–12.7, is split rather than fused: לְ takes *in*, עַיִן takes *sight*, the suffix takes *their*. The ASV spends a word on each morpheme, so rule 30's one-English-word condition is unmet and rule 2 governs; do not read *in the sight of* as one rendering.

The ethical dative לְךָ / לִי on an imperative or a first-person verb (12.3, 12.5, 12.7): the preposition is `unrepresented` in every case under rule 40, and its suffix takes an English pronoun only where the ASV writes one — *thee* in *prepare thee stuff* (12.3), nothing in *Dig thou through the wall* (12.5) or *I digged* (12.7). The *thou* of *Dig thou* and of *Say thou* (12.10) is the imperative's own subject pronoun under rule 17 and is never the suffix's. BSB represents these prepositions and suffixes; that is the convention difference the validation report counts.

בֵּית הַמֶּרִי is rendered attributively throughout (rule 28), and the article's placement follows what the ASV writes. Where the ASV writes two *the*s (12.2 *the midst of the rebellious house*, 12.9 *the house of Israel the rebellious house*), the article takes the one standing before its own word's rendering *rebellious* and the construct noun takes a supplied one, per rule 29's arthrous-rectum clause; nothing is fronted. In the vocative *O rebellious house* (12.25) the ASV writes no *the* at all, so the article is `unrepresented` and the noun holds the whole *O … house* under rule 36.

כַּאֲשֶׁר is deliberately treated two ways in this chapter and neither is to be harmonised to the other: fused into one unit for the single *as* of 12.7, split into *like* (כְּ) and *as* (אֲשֶׁר) in 12.11, where the ASV spends a word on each morpheme. Rule 30's one-English-word condition, not the Hebrew phrase, decides which.

report: Read all 44 candidate lemma groups and the full dump end to end. No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source to license the difference, so patches is empty.

Pairs that look like splits and are not: כַּאֲשֶׁר fused to *as* in v.7 and split *like*/*as* in v.11, rule 30's one-English-word condition being met in one and not the other; the assimilated article of בָעֶרֶב unrepresented in v.4 (*at even*) and aligned in v.7 (*in the even*), per rule 29's 'only where the ASV writes no the'; אֲלֵיהֶם unrepresented in v.23 (*Tell them*) and aligned in v.10 and later in v.23 (*say unto them*), per rule 40.

Supplied possessives are the sharpest test, and one verse carries both outcomes on purpose: v.12 marks *his* on כָּתֵף `added` (t011, no article and no suffix stands) and aligns *his* on לַ[הַ]עַיִן to the article (t043, rule 41). v.6 and v.7 treat their unsuffixed כָּתֵף and יָד exactly as t011.

Supplied subordinators are consistent in principle rather than by accident. כְּ takes *as when* in v.4 because a preposition heads the phrase the ASV recasts as a clause (rule 52's closing sentence, which reads the preposition present rather than its lemma), while v.22's *that* is `added` because that clause holds no conjunction and its לְ has already spent its English on *have* (rule 46's third limit, decided under 55). Four supplied *that*s go four ways — article present to the article (v.20), articleless attributive to the attributive (v.27), recast substantive with no antecedent into the substantive (v.19 מְלֹא), finite clause beside a written antecedent `added` (v.22) — which is exactly what rules 41, 46 and 55 distinguish.

The candidate table is keyed by source lemma and so cannot see `added` units; I read those separately. Fifteen, in five families, each handled identically wherever it recurs: supplied object pronouns with no object morpheme (v.6 x2, v.7 x2), supplied possessives (v.6, v.7 x2, v.12), supplied coordinating *and* with no waw present (v.6 t011, v.7 t039, v.19 t019), wholly supplied lexical verbs (v.10 *concerneth*, v.19 *and despoiled*), and one supplied subordinator (v.22 t008).

The v.19 correction already on disk — אֶל `unrepresented` and *and* `added` — is what brings the third member of the supplied-*and* family into line with the other two. Before it, that verse folded the coordinator into a neighbouring preposition, which is the error the amendment below is meant to stop.

Heads were reviewed independently of edges. בְּתוֹךְ is fused in v.10, v.12 and v.24 with identical heads (source on תָּוֶךְ, target on the English preposition), the v.10 note's 'heads on the preposition' referring to the English word as rule 49 does. Every light-verb unit heads on its complement (*waste* v.20, *cease* v.23, *hand* v.23, *proverb* v.23) and every phrasal particle leaves the head on the verb (*forth*, *out* in v.4, 5, 7, 12, 14).

BSB: all 32 disagreements fall in documented convention families — unrendered prepositions under rules 27 and 40 (the R x 10 group and the ethical datives), object markers under 16, the אֲדֹנָי suffix, and articles under 29, 41, 47 and 36. None is a genuine error, and no accepted edge was changed.
Recorded five conventions covering the recurring judgments the 73 repeated verse notes were carrying without a log entry, and one amendment to rule 14.
